subject: physics
question_text: Why are drops and bubbles spherical?

mark_split.label: The sphere has the least area

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2024 (Q6) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: surface tension T is numerically equal to the surface energy per unit area, so the work needed to increase the area by ΔA is W = T × ΔA; a free liquid mass settles at the state of least surface energy, which is the state of least surface area; for a fixed volume the sphere is the shape of least surface area. Large drops resting on a surface are flattened because their weight is no longer small beside the surface tension forces.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Link surface tension to surface energy through W = T × ΔA.
steps.why: Surface tension and surface energy are the same quantity: T is force per unit length and also energy per unit area. The shape then follows from the energy being least.
common_mistakes: Saying the air outside presses the drop into a ball. The cause is the liquid's own surface tension.
Saying the surface area becomes zero. The volume is fixed, so the area has a smallest possible value, not a zero one.

recall.must_convey: That surface tension means a larger area costs more energy, so a free drop settles at the least surface area.
accept: work is T into delta A
reject: a sphere has the least area for a given volume

steps.memory_tip: Surface tension is energy per unit area, so least area means least energy.

lines.text: Least area for a given volume: the sphere

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the sphere as the least-area shape for a fixed volume.
steps.why: This is the geometrical half of the answer. Without it the first step says only that the area is small, never why the shape is a ball.
common_mistakes: Claiming every drop is spherical. A large drop on a table is flattened by its own weight.
Saying a sphere has the largest volume for a given area and leaving it there. State it the way the question needs: least area for a given volume.

recall.must_convey: That for a given volume the sphere has the smallest surface area, so drops and bubbles are spherical.
accept: sphere has the least surface area
reject: work is T into delta A

steps.memory_tip: Fixed volume, smallest area: the sphere. That one fact ends the answer.

insider_note: Two statements, one mark each: surface tension reduces the area, and the sphere is the least-area shape for a given volume. Students omit the second.
